title: Safety Alert: Hazira gas terminal condensate release and fire, 2020
status: Learning purposes: not a statutory document

incident.title: Hazira gas terminal condensate release and fire

data_quality.text: Draft learnings from an unreviewed analysis: the export's investigation status is in progress and no finding is marked as edited by a person. Validate every item before this alert is shared beyond the site.

bottom_line.text: A seal that does not match the original specification is a change, not a spare.
An opened pressure joint is not proven until it passes a recorded test to design pressure.
Work that can cause a major release needs a check by someone other than the person doing it.

items.text: On 24 September 2020 condensate vapour escaped from a seal on a 1986 metering skid at a gas terminal, six days after the seal had been replaced [FND-8C0BB623; EVD-8645]. The vapour cloud spread for about 46 minutes before the first isolation valve was closed by hand [FND-322112EE; EVD-6414]. It then ignited at a damaged flameproof light fitting and caused a major fire [FND-CCE6F868; EVD-6916].

All three learnings apply industry-wide. Any site with legacy pressure equipment, locally bought spares or maintenance run on a work notification alone can hold the same conditions today [FND-2FAB8D51; FND-7C5ED5B3; EVD-8645].

items.lesson: If the specification for a pressure-boundary part is lost and no role owns it, crews fit whatever part is to hand, and the substitute becomes normal practice.
items.explanation: Locally bought O-rings replaced a slot gasket with no specification, check or approval; the seal fitted on 18 September failed six days later.

items.lesson: If no procedure says how an opened high-pressure joint is tested before service, crews use the quickest check, and a weak joint passes.
items.explanation: The joint was pressurised only to operating pressure, with no test to design pressure, and went back online about 46 hours later.

items.lesson: If a job that can cause a major release is planned like routine work, the fitter's knowledge is the only barrier.
items.explanation: No one was assigned to check the part, the method or the test.

items.text: Do not return an opened pressure-boundary joint to service until a recorded test to design pressure has passed.
List the pressure-boundary seals on legacy equipment that have no specification on file.
Ask stores whether a pressure-boundary seal can be issued without a specification reference.
Check whether safety-critical maintenance jobs carry an independent check of part, method and test.

items.question: When you change a seal, how do you know the new one matches the original specification?
items.why: Shows whether the specification is on file or held only in people's memory.

items.question: What test does a joint you opened pass before it goes back into service, and who sees the result?
items.why: Shows whether the test is written down and checked by someone other than the fitter.

items.text: Send questions, and what your checks find, to the site process-safety lead.

limits: The alert carries the three priority-1 learnings the engine chose by default (alert-grade); the register holds eight more priority-1 learnings, on emergency response, isolation, gas detection, hazardous-area equipment and competence.
